copy.en: "Tsunami" is a Japanese word meaning "harbor wave." It got this name because these giant waves often crash into and damage harbors!
copy.tl: Ang "tsunami" ay salitang Hapon na ibig sabihin ay "alon sa daungan." Tinawag ito ganoon dahil madalas bumagsak at sumira ang mga alon sa mga daungan!
copy.bis: Ang "tsunami" pulong Hapon nga nagpasabot og "balod sa pantalan." Gitawag niini tungod kay kasagaran mokras ug makaguba ang mga dako nga balod sa mga pantalan!

copy.en: A tsunami is different from normal wind waves! Regular waves only move the surface, but a tsunami moves the whole water column from bottom to top—making it much more powerful!
copy.tl: Iba ang tsunami sa karaniwang alon na gawa ng hangin! Ang normal na alon ay nasa ibabaw lang, pero ang tsunami ay galaw ng buong tubig mula ilalim hanggang itaas—kaya mas malakas ito!
copy.bis: Lahi ang tsunami sa ordinaryong balod nga gibuhat sa hangin! Ang ordinaryong balod naa ra sa ibabaw, apan ang tsunami molihok sa tibuok tubig gikan sa ilalom hangtod sa taas—maong mas kusog kini!

copy.en: In the deep ocean, a tsunami travels as fast as a jet plane! Yet it stays so low that you would barely notice it from a ship.
copy.tl: Sa malalim na karagatan, napakabilis ng tsunami—kasimbilis ng jet plane! Pero mababa pa rin ito kaya halos hindi mo ito mapapansin mula sa barko.
copy.bis: Sa lawom nga kadagatan, kusog kaayo modagan ang tsunami—sama kapaspas sa jet plane! Apan ubos gihapon kini maong halos dili nimo mamatikdan gikan sa barko.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In the deep middle of the ocean, tsunami waves are actually very low!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how earthquakes result in tsunamis that devastate shoreline communities
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about tsunami wave height in deep water, but does not mention earthquakes, how they generate tsunamis, or how tsunamis devastate shoreline communities. It is only tangentially related to the competency's subject.

copy.en: In the deep middle of the ocean, tsunami waves are actually very low! Ships sailing by might not even notice them at all.
copy.tl: Sa gitna ng karagatan, ang alon ng tsunami ay mababa lang! Kaya maaaring hindi ito mapansin ng mga barkong dumadaan.
copy.bis: Sa tunga sa kadagatan, ang mga balod sa tsunami ubos ra! Mao nga basin dili kini mamatikdan sa mga barkong nagabyahe.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A tsunami is not made by the tides or the moon
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how earthquakes result in tsunamis that devastate shoreline communities
assignedReviews.reason: The card only clarifies that a tsunami is not a tidal wave, but does not explain how earthquakes result in tsunamis or their devastation of shoreline communities, which is the core of the competency.

copy.en:
Is a tsunami the same thing as a tidal wave?

A tsunami is not made by the tides or the moon, so it is actually wrong to call it a tidal wave!
copy.tl:
Ang tsunami ba ay pareho sa tidal wave?

Ang tsunami ay hindi gawa ng taog o ng buwan, kaya hindi ito tamang tawaging tidal wave!
copy.bis:
Ang tsunami ba pareho sa tidal wave?

Ang tsunami dili hinimo sa taob o sa bulan, mao nga sayop ang pagtawag niini ug tidal wave!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The danger of a tsunami is not just the wave height, but the strong rushing current that sweeps away people and houses!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how earthquakes result in tsunamis that devastate shoreline communities
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses tsunami danger but does not explain how earthquakes result in tsunamis or how they devastate shoreline communities. It only mentions the destructive current, not the earthquake-tsunami mechanism.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The danger of a tsunami is not just the wave height, but the strong rushing current that sweeps away people and houses!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how the effects of earthquakes on communities depend on their magnitude
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe how earthquake effects on communities depend on magnitude. It is about tsunami danger, unrelated to earthquake magnitude.

copy.en: The danger of a tsunami is not just the wave height, but the strong rushing current that sweeps away people and houses!
copy.tl: Ang panganib ng tsunami ay hindi lang ang taas ng alon, kundi ang malakas na agos na nakakatangay ng tao at bahay!
copy.bis: Ang peligro sa tsunami dili lang ang gitas-on sa balod, kondili ang kusog nga sulog nga makabanlas sa tawo ug balay!

copy.en: A tuber is a thick, enlarged underground stem with tiny buds called eyes, and sweet potato or kamote is an example.
copy.tl: Ang tuber ay makapal at lumaking underground stem na may maliliit na buds na tinatawag na eyes, at halimbawa nito ang kamote.
copy.bis: Ang tuber baga ug dako nga underground stem nga adunay gagmay nga buds nga gitawag og eyes, ug pananglitan ang kamote.

copy.en: The tuna is one of the fastest fish in the sea — it can zoom through the water at incredible speed.
copy.tl: Ang tuna ay isa sa pinakamabilis na isda sa dagat — kayang lumangoy nito nang napakabilis.
copy.bis: Ang tuna usa sa labing paspas nga isda sa dagat — makalanguy kini og kusog kaayo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some tuna species use a special heat-exchange system to keep their muscles warmer than the water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a current physiological feature (heat-exchange system) that helps tuna swim faster, but it does not describe how the animal changed over time to better suit its environment, nor does it use mimicry/camouflage-type adaptation language. It is only related to the broad topic of animal features suiting their environment.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some tuna species use a special heat-exchange system to keep their muscles warmer than the water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about how human body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work. The card is about tuna heat exchange and swimming, not any human body system, so it does not support this competency.

copy.en:
Which fish can keep its muscles warmer than the water?

Some tuna species use a special heat-exchange system to keep their muscles warmer than the water, letting them swim faster than most fish.
copy.tl:
Aling isda ang kayang panatilihing mainit ang kalamnan?

Ang ilang uri ng tuna ay gumagamit ng espesyal na heat-exchange system para panatilihing mas mainit ang kanilang kalamnan kaysa tubig, kaya sila mas mabilis lumangoy kaysa karamihang isda.
copy.bis:
Unsang isda ang makahimo pabilin nga init ang kalamnan?

Ang pipila ka klase sa tuna naggamit og espesyal nga heat-exchange system aron mapabilin nga mas init ang ilang kalamnan kaysa tubig, mao nga mas paspas sila molangoy kaysa kadaghanan sa isda.

copy.en: Turmeric isn't just for cooking — it's also used as a natural yellow dye for cloth because it stains so strongly!
copy.tl: Hindi lang pang-pagkain ang luyang dilaw — ginagamit din itong likas na pangkulay ng tela dahil malakas itong magmantsa ng dilaw!
copy.bis: Dili lang para sa pagkaon ang luyang dilaw — gigamit usab kini nga natural nga tina sa panapton kay kusog kini momansa og dalag!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A turtle's shell is part of its body and connected to its bones
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (the shell) but its stated role is protection, not movement or gathering food as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it's armor the turtle can hide inside when danger comes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a protective adaptation but does not describe how the shell is a change that better suits the environment, nor does it use secondary sources or address mimicry/camouflage.

copy.en: A turtle's shell is part of its body and connected to its bones — it's armor the turtle can hide inside when danger comes.
copy.tl: Ang talukab ng pagong ay bahagi ng kanyang katawan at nakakabit sa kanyang buto — ito ang kalasag na pinagtataguan niya kapag may panganib.
copy.bis: Ang bagol sa baw kabahin sa iyang lawas ug konektado sa iyang mga bukog — mao kini ang kalasag nga iyang gisuksokan kon adunay kuyaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dragonflies are older!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the geologic time scale helps to recount the history of the Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single fact about dragonflies predating dinosaurs but does not explain the geologic time scale or how it helps recount Earth's history. It only touches on ancient life, which is related to Earth history but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
Which is older, dragonflies or dinosaurs?

Dragonflies are older! They are an ancient kind of insect that was already flying on Earth even before the dinosaurs existed.
copy.tl:
Alin ang mas matanda, tutubi o dinosaur?

Ang tutubi! Ito ay isang matandang uri ng insekto na lumilipad na sa mundo bago pa dumating ang mga dinosauro.
copy.bis:
Hain ang mas karaan, alindahaw o dinosaur?

Ang alindahaw! Kini usa ka karaan nga matang sa insekto nga naglupad na sa kalibotan sa wala pa ang mga dinosauro.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: eating small water animals like tadpoles and tiny fish
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a dragonfly nymph's diet but does not group animals into herbivores, carnivores, or omnivores, nor does it use secondary sources as required by the competency.

copy.en: The underwater young dragonfly is a skilled hunter too, eating small water animals like tadpoles and tiny fish.
copy.tl: Mahusay ding mangaso ang batang tutubi sa ilalim ng tubig — kumakain ito ng maliliit na hayop tulad ng butete at maliliit na isda.
copy.bis: Hanas usab mangayam ang batan-ong alindahaw ilalom sa tubig — mokaon kini og gagmayng mananap sama sa uok ug gagmayng isda.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: two ears really help — a blaring horn instantly tells you if it's from your left, right, or behind
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses sound localization using two ears, not how sound is made or transferred. It does not support the competency's focus on sound production and transmission in everyday situations.

copy.en: On busy Philippine streets full of jeepneys and cars, two ears really help — a blaring horn instantly tells you if it's from your left, right, or behind.
copy.tl: Sa magulong kalsada ng Pilipinas na puno ng jeepney at sasakyan, malaking tulong ang dalawang tainga — agad mong malalaman kung saan nanggaling ang busina.
copy.bis: Sa gubot nga dalan sa Pilipinas nga puno sa jeepney ug sakyanan, dako'g tabang ang duha ka dalunggan — dayon mahibaloan kon asa gikan ang bosina.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Our two eyes are set apart, so each sees a slightly different view — the brain combines them so we can judge depth and distance.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes eyes and their role in depth perception, but G3-L-4 focuses on outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings and their role in movement and gathering food. Eyes and depth perception do not directly support that competency.

copy.en:
Why do we need two eyes to see depth?

Our two eyes are set apart, so each sees a slightly different view — the brain combines them so we can judge depth and distance.
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangan ng dalawang mata para makita ang lalim?

Dahil magkahiwalay ang ating dalawang mata, bahagyang magkaiba ang nakikita ng bawat isa — pinagsasama ito ng utak para masukat natin ang lalim at layo ng mga bagay.
copy.bis:
Ngano kinahanglan ang duha ka mata aron makita ang giladmon?

Tungod kay magkalain ang atong duha ka mata, gamay nga lahi ang makita sa matag usa — gihiusa kini sa utok aron matakos nato ang giladmon ug gilay-on sa mga butang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You have two bean-shaped kidneys tucked in the back of your belly, close to your spine!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the location and shape of the kidneys. It does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, nor does it explain how body systems work together (e.g., digestion and excretion). The kidney is part of the excretory system, but the card provides no information about system interactions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You have two bean-shaped kidneys tucked in the back of your belly, close to your spine!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a body part (kidney) but does not describe how any of the listed body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work. It gives no functional information about the kidney or any system, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: You have two bean-shaped kidneys tucked in the back of your belly, close to your spine!
copy.tl: May dalawang bato ang tao na hugis-balatong, nasa likod ng tiyan, malapit sa gulugod!
copy.bis: Ang tawo adunay duha ka kidney nga porma sa balatong, nahimutang sa luyo sa tiyan, duol sa bukog sa likod!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: each cell naturally carries both A and B antigens
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of DNA, genes, and chromosomes in the transmission of traits
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that type AB blood cells carry both A and B antigens, which is a fact about blood type expression. However, it does not explain the role of DNA, genes, or chromosomes in transmitting traits. It does not discuss how genes encode antigens or how traits are inherited. The content is only tangentially related to genetics and does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: each cell naturally carries both A and B antigens
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: represent patterns of inheritance of a simple dominant/ recessive characteristic through generations of a family
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses the nature of type AB blood, which is an example of codominance, not a simple dominant/recessive characteristic. It does not represent patterns of inheritance through generations of a family, nor does it discuss dominant/recessive traits. The card provides no information about family pedigrees or inheritance patterns, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
Is type AB blood a mix of A and B?

No! Type AB is its own complete blood type, not two bloods mixed together — each cell naturally carries both A and B antigens.
copy.tl:
Halo ba ng type A at B ang type AB?

Hindi! Ang type AB ay sariling buong blood type, hindi ito pinaghalong dugo — likas na may A at B antigen ang bawat selula.
copy.bis:
Sagol ba sa type A ug B ang type AB?

Dili! Ang type AB kaugalingon nga kompleto nga blood type, dili duha ka dugo nga gisagol — natural nga adunay A ug B antigen ang matag selula.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Even people with blood type AB have one more question to answer — Rh positive or negative
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: ABO/Rh typing is matching, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That makes AB+ and AB-, and AB+ is the true universal recipient
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: represent patterns of inheritance of a simple dominant/ recessive characteristic through generations of a family
assignedReviews.reason: Rh positive versus negative is not representing inheritance of a dominant/recessive characteristic through generations of a family.

copy.en: Even people with blood type AB have one more question to answer — Rh positive or negative. That makes AB+ and AB-, and AB+ is the true universal recipient, able to receive blood from anyone.
copy.tl: Kahit ang may blood type AB ay may isa pang dapat malaman — Rh positive o negative. Kaya may AB+ at AB-, at ang AB+ ang tunay na universal recipient na puwedeng tumanggap ng dugo mula kahit kanino.
copy.bis: Bisan ang adunay blood type AB naa pay usa ka butang nga masayran — Rh positive o negative. Mao nga naa'y AB+ ug AB-, ug ang AB+ mao ang tinuod nga universal recipient nga makadawat og dugo gikan bisan kinsa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Galaxies come in three main types: spiral (with spiral arms like ours), elliptical (egg-shaped and older), and irregular (with no defined shape)!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about the general structure of the solar system and its major celestial objects (Sun, planets, etc.). assignedReviews.card_evidence: Galaxies come in three main types: spiral (with spiral arms like ours), elliptical (egg-shaped and older), and irregular (with no defined shape)!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The competency focuses on observing and describing natural objects seen in the sky, specifically the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars. Galaxies are not among these objects and are not typically observed as individual objects in daytime/nighttime sky activities at Grade 3. The card shares the broad astronomy topic but does not directly support the listed objects or guided observation activities.

copy.en:
What are the three main types of galaxies?

Galaxies come in three main types: spiral (with spiral arms like ours), elliptical (egg-shaped and older), and irregular (with no defined shape)!
copy.tl:
Ano ang tatlong pangunahing uri ng mga galaxy?

Ang mga galaxy ay may tatlong pangunahing uri: spiral (may spiral arms tulad ng Milky Way), elliptical (hugis itlog at mas matanda), at irregular (walang tiyak na hugis)!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang tulo ka panguna nga klase sa mga galaxy?

Ang mga galaxy adunay tulo ka panguna nga klase: spiral (may spiral arms sama sa Milky Way), elliptical (hugis itlog ug mas tigulang), ug irregular (walay tinuding hugis)!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: These features only show up when the storm spins strong and fast enough.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain: a. how typhoons develop, and b. why the Philippines is prone to typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the presence of an eye and eyewall based on storm intensity, which is a structural feature of typhoons. It does not explain how typhoons develop or why the Philippines is prone to typhoons, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Weak storms and tropical depressions usually lack a clear eyewall.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a condition during a tropical cyclone (lack of clear eyewall in weak storms), but it does not describe typical weather conditions before, during, or after a tropical cyclone. It is only tangentially related to storm characteristics.

copy.en: Not every storm has a clear eye and eyewall! These features only show up when the storm spins strong and fast enough. Weak storms and tropical depressions usually lack a clear eyewall.
copy.tl: Hindi lahat ng bagyo ay may malinaw na mata at eyewall! Lumalabas lang ang mga ito kapag sapat na ang lakas at bilis ng bagyo. Ang mahihinang bagyo o tropical depression ay madalas walang malinaw na eyewall pa.
copy.bis: Dili tanan bagyo adunay tin-aw nga mata ug eyewall! Motungha lang kini kung kusog ug paspas na ang paglikolik sa bagyo. Ang huyang nga bagyo o tropical depression kasagaran walay tin-aw nga eyewall pa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they all have an eyewall
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that typhoons, hurricanes, and cyclones all have an eyewall. It does not describe typical weather conditions before, during, or after a tropical cyclone, which is the focus of G5-E-10.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they all have an eyewall
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain: a. how typhoons develop, and b. why the Philippines is prone to typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions typhoons but does not explain how typhoons develop or why the Philippines is prone to typhoons. It only gives a general fact about the eyewall, so it does not directly support G8-E-7.

copy.en:
Do hurricanes and cyclones have an eyewall too?

Yes! Whether it's a typhoon, hurricane, or cyclone, they all have an eyewall. The name just changes by region, but the science behind the eyewall is exactly the same!
copy.tl:
May eyewall din ba ang mga hurricane at cyclone?

Oo! Typhoon man, hurricane, o cyclone, lahat sila may eyewall. Nag-iiba lang ang pangalan depende sa lugar, pero iisa ang agham sa likod ng eyewall!
copy.bis:
Aduna ba bay eyewall ang mga hurricane ug cyclone?

Oo! Typhoon man, hurricane, o cyclone, tanan adunay eyewall. Lahi lang ang ngalan base sa lugar, apan parehas ra ang siyensya luyo sa eyewall!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: But they are weaker than the eyewall, which remains the innermost and strongest ring!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the internal structure of a tropical cyclone (rainbands vs. eyewall) and their relative strength. The competency requires describing typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone. The card does not address the sequence of weather conditions or the typical conditions at each phase; it only provides a structural fact about the storm's anatomy, which is not directly instructional for the stated skill.

copy.en: Farther out, spiraling rain stripes called rainbands swirl around the storm. But they are weaker than the eyewall, which remains the innermost and strongest ring!
copy.tl: Mas malayo, may mga papaikot na guhit ng ulan na rainbands. Pero mas mahina sila kaysa eyewall, na nananatiling pinakaloob at pinakamalakas na singsing ng bagyo!
copy.bis: Mas layo, adunay naglikoliko nga gilis sa ulan nga rainbands. Pero mas huyang kini kay sa eyewall, nga nagpabilin nga pinakasulod ug pinakakusog nga singsing sa bagyo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Every typhoon entering the Philippines gets its own special name.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal issued by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geological and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA)
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why PAGASA names typhoons, but does not describe weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal. It only shares the agency name and a general fact about naming, not the signal-based weather description required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Every typhoon entering the Philippines gets its own special name.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a map and a record of tracking data to trace the path of typhoons that enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions typhoons entering the Philippines, but does not involve using a map or tracking data to trace typhoon paths. Naming typhoons is not the same as tracing their path, so it provides no direct instructional support for this competency.

copy.en:
Why does PAGASA give names to typhoons?

So we can easily spot them and follow the news! Every typhoon entering the Philippines gets its own special name.
copy.tl:
